title: Songbook and Garden
premise: Vesper Winterbourne keeps her late grandfather's lighthouse on the Cornish coast and writes novels nobody buys, convinced she squandered her one great love a decade ago. When a snowstorm traps her with Julian Ashcombe — the composer who was her best mistake at twenty-two — and his ruthless business rival Marguerite Vane, who wants to buy and demolish the lighthouse, old songs, buried letters, and a contested inheritance force all three into confession. As the storm strips away their defenses, Vesper discovers her grandfather willed her the choice, not the obligation, to keep the light. She forgives herself, chooses Julian without abandoning her own voice, and turns the lighthouse into a songbook-and-garden retreat that belongs to all of them.
about_author: Jude Brightwater is the pen name of a former coastal archivist who spent seven years cataloguing shipwreck letters before turning to fiction. They write romance about people who inherit more than property.

chapters.title: The Light That Waits
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper tends the lighthouse alone on the winter solstice, cataloguing her grandfather's effects and dodging a letter from the Vane Development Group. A flashback shows her walking out on Julian ten years ago in London. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment, and the first crack of regret.

chapters.title: Two Cars in the Snow
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A whiteout strands two cars below the cliff road: Julian Ashcombe, en route to sign papers elsewhere, and Marguerite Vane, arriving to close the lighthouse purchase. Vesper hauls both up through the snow. Emotional beat: shock and unwilling tenderness as Julian says her name like a chord resolving.

chapters.title: Three at Supper
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Trapped by the storm, the three share supper; Marguerite reveals she grew up in the village the lighthouse once guided home. Julian watches Vesper laugh and realizes he never stopped composing for her. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by guilt over what he became after she left.

chapters.title: The Songbook in the Wall
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Repairing storm damage, Vesper finds her grandfather's hidden songbook — folk tunes annotated in two hands: his and, impossibly, young Julian's, from a summer he never mentioned. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into curiosity; the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Terms
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite offers Vesper a generous buyout and admits the demolition will erase the last building tied to her own childhood. When Vesper hesitates, Marguerite deploys the contract clause her lawyers hid. Emotional beat: sympathy weaponized; power showing its teeth.

chapters.title: What He Wrote Instead
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confesses the summer he spent here at nineteen, learning folk tunes from Vesper's grandfather after his own father disowned him — and that he sold those melodies early in his career. Vesper overhears half of it. Emotional beat: honesty offered too late, misread as another betrayal.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Alone in the lamp room during the storm's peak, Vesper rereads her grandfather's final letter: he knew she'd run from Julian, knew she'd punish herself, and left her the lighthouse precisely so she'd have somewhere to stop running. Emotional beat: the turning point — self-forgiveness begins.

chapters.title: Climax: The Clause Breaks
chapters.summary: All three POVs interleave. At dawn Marguerite arrives with the signed transfer; Vesper invokes the inheritance clause her grandfather embedded — the deed passes only to an heir who keeps the light burning, which voids the sale. Julian publicly renounces the melodies' royalties to the songbook archive. Emotional beat: collision of power, love, and legacy at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The storm breaks. Marguerite, defeated but unburdened, walks the cliff path her mother once walked and asks instead to fund the restoration. Julian plays the grandfather's unfinished tune on the lamp room floor while Vesper harmonizes. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into alliance; rivals becoming kin.

chapters.title: Songbook and Garden
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. One year later: the lighthouse is a retreat where musicians transcribe the songbook and villagers tend terraced gardens down the cliff. Vesper finishes her novel, kisses Julian in the doorway, and lights the lamp each dusk — not because she must, but because she chose to. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance redefined, second chances kept.
